top_band: terracotta/red-brown tiled roof slope from row 2 to row 43 (lightest at the ridge rows 3-13, darkening toward the eave)
evidence: Rows 2-43 show the full foreshortened roof slope with ridge cap and chimney top opening (row 1). Row 42-43 forms the eave edge, overhanging the vertical timber-and-plaster front wall at rows 44-78, with eave shadow at rows 44-45 and recessed door/window.

style.evidence: While the roof has multiple shading steps and plaster has speckle, the textures and forms are noticeably boxier, simpler, and more blocky than the Beodeul reference: roof tiles are 4x4 flat blocks instead of fine 2x2 diagonal/scalloped tiles, the door is a simple 4-plank vector-like arch without fine wood grain, window glass uses thick 2px diagonal stripes, and timber framing lacks diagonal braces and fine edge shading.
